questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Kid', why did the Kid stay behind when the flock went home?
choices: His growing horns made him think he could take care of himself
He had wandered into the woods and could not find the path back
His mother told him to wait by the clump of trees until morning
He was too tired from frisking all day to walk home with the flock
questions.evidence: whose growing horns made him think he was a grown-up Billy Goat

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Kid', what did the Kid ask the Wolf to do before eating him?
choices: Pipe him a tune so he could dance
Let him run home and say goodbye to his mother
Tell him a story about the Shepherd Dogs
Let him nibble one last bite of tender grass
questions.evidence: first please pipe me a tune

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Kid', how did the Wolf's music save the Kid?
choices: The Shepherd Dogs heard it and came running
It put the Wolf to sleep so the Kid could slip away
It was so loud that it frightened the Wolf himself
The Kid's mother heard it and came back for him
questions.evidence: The Shepherd Dogs pricked up their ears

questions.q: In 'The Tortoise and the Ducks', how did the Ducks carry the Tortoise into the air?
choices: He held a stick in his teeth while they held the ends
He rode on the back of the biggest Duck in the flock
They carried him between them in a basket of reeds
They gripped the edges of his shell with their feet
questions.evidence: Take hold of this stick with your teeth

questions.q: In 'The Tortoise and the Ducks', what made the Tortoise fall?
choices: He opened his mouth to answer the Crow
The Ducks grew tired and let go of the stick
The stick snapped in two above the treetops
He fell asleep and loosened his hold on the stick
questions.evidence: as he opened his mouth to say these foolish words he lost his hold on the stick

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Young Crab and His Mother'?
choices: Set a good example before you tell others how to act
Always walk straight forward and never sideways
Children should obey their mothers in everything
Slow and steady walking wins in the end
questions.evidence: Do not tell others how to act unless you can set a good example.

questions.q: In 'The Frogs and the Ox', what happened to the old Frog in the end?
choices: She puffed herself up until she burst
She hopped away from the Ox into the water
She grew until she was as big as the Ox
She was stepped on when the Ox came to drink

questions.q: What lesson does 'The Frogs and the Ox' teach?
choices: Do not attempt the impossible
Always tell your children the truth
Big animals are always mean to small ones
Stay away from the pond when an Ox is near
